- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to compensate for bearish sentiment bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overreacts and forecasts a prolonged overshoot; reduce forecast peak by 3–5% and add a slight downward slope to avoid overcorrection.
- If model forecast mean is significantly below true outcome mean (e.g., >3% gap), apply a “mean reversion” correction: add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for the next 3–5 days to align with recent upward momentum.
- When sentiment swings from negative to positive (e.g., +0.3+ in 3–5 days), model often lags in recognizing the shift; increase forecast slope by 0.1–0.3% per day to capture sentiment-driven rebound.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period volatility (last 7–10 days); apply a “volatility bump” correction: add 0.5–1.5% to final 5–7 days of forecast to reflect sentiment-driven breakout potential.
